subject: Bridging inference environments: network connector options and recommendation
messages:
From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@datasynchealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment connectivity — quick ask

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to picking a private deployment pattern for our inference tier and want a practical recommendation from Redwood. High level constraints:
- Primary infra is AWS (us-east-1) with an on-prem datacenter for PCI systems.
- Must be HIPAA-friendly; our security team requires strict traffic segmentation and auditability.
- Expected peak is ~600 concurrent streams, steady-state ~150 qps.
- We need a path that supports rollout across dev/stage/prod (isolation per env).
- Timeline: POC in two weeks, production in ~3 months.

Specifically can you advise tradeoffs between VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink (Interface endpoints), and a Site-to-Site VPN (or Direct Connect)? Also any red flags for cross-account peering or when to use Transit Gateway?

I've attached the RFP draft and our network topology diagram. Appreciate a short write-up + recommended next steps.

Best,
Carlos
Senior Infrastructure Lead
DataSync Health

Attachments: RFP_datasync_health.pdf
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@datasynchealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — quick ask

Hi Carlos — thanks for the context and the diagram. Below is a concise recommendation and the tradeoffs so you can pick the fastest safe path for the POC and a more robust plan for production. I included an attachment with a simple diagram and a cost/ops row-by-row CSV.

Recommendation summary (TL;DR):
- POC: Interface PrivateLink (Redwood Private exposes an Interface VPC Endpoint in your VPC) + short-lived Site-to-Site VPN fallback. PrivateLink gives per-service access, minimal route table changes, and easier least-privilege controls for HIPAA-sensitive flows.
- Production: AWS Direct Connect with Transit Gateway + PrivateLink endpoints for segmented services, or Peering only if all resources are in the same account and you can accept transitive limitations.

Tradeoffs and notes:
1) VPC Peering
   - Pros: Low latency, simple (if same account or between accounts in same region), no extra proxies.
   - Cons: No transitive routing (hard to scale across many VPCs/regions), harder to lock down to per-service ports (broad network access), route table sprawl. For multi-account corporate setups peering becomes operationally heavy. Not recommended as the only strategy for HIPAA-sensitive, multi-environment deployments unless you standardize a small number of peered VPCs.

2) AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints)
   - Pros: Service-level access (good for least privilege), flows stay inside AWS backbone, easy to audit per-endpoint, works cross-account, simpler security posture for regulated data. Supports NLB in front of Redwood Private if needed. Scales cleanly for many accounts/environments.
   - Cons: Per-endpoint ENIs and ENI limits on smaller instance types; slightly higher per-GB cost than peering. Requires managing interface endpoints per VPC but avoids complex route propagation.

3) Site-to-Site VPN / Direct Connect
   - VPN Pros: Fastest to stand up for a POC; full network access; can be encrypted using your edge devices.
   - VPN Cons: Variable latency, operational overhead (BGP), and if you use full-mesh VPNs it increases blast radius. For production at scale, prefer Direct Connect with Transit Gateway for stable throughput and predictable egress pricing.

Operational & security considerations
- For HIPAA: enforce TLS+mTLS to the Redwood runtime, restrict access at the PrivateLink/NACL/security-group layer, and enable flow-logging plus host-level audit collection.
- Routing: prefer Transit Gateway when you have >3 VPCs or multi-account needs; it simplifies routing and supports central inspection.
- Fallbacks: design a fallback policy in the Redwood Console: primary=PrivateLink, fallback=VPN, fail-open only if explicitly allowed.
- Monitoring & SLOs: capture token-level latency and per-route cost in the Console. We'll surface anomalies if the P99 deviates.

Next steps I propose:
1) POC plan (2 weeks): we set up a PrivateLink endpoint with an NLB in your staging VPC + a site-to-site VPN for failover. Redwood will provide a small config repo and the network diagram.
2) Security review: our security engineer (Rishi) can join your security call for the HIPAA checklist.
3) Production design doc: after POC, iterate to Direct Connect + Transit Gateway if throughput or predictable latency is required.

If that sounds good I'll send an action plan with dates.

Best,
Naomi
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — quick ask

Adding a couple of ops/security specifics from my side:

- Encryption: enforce TLS 1.2+ with client certs (we can provide a managed cert rotation option for PrivateLink mTLS).
- ENI/IP quotas: confirm your account ENI limits in the staging VPC (PrivateLink will create ENIs per AZ). If quotas are tight we can either request a quota bump or use an NLB-backed pattern that reduces ENI usage.
- Transit Gateway note: if you intend to share the same Redwood Private across multiple AWS accounts, use TGW in hub-and-spoke + PrivateLink for service isolation; avoids per-account peering complexity.
- Metrics: we'll enable per-endpoint telemetry in the Console (latency histograms, egress count, per-token cost) so you can tie regressions to network path changes.

Operational checklist for the POC (I can own these items with Naomi):
- Week 0 (this week): confirm VPC IDs, account numbers, expected qps, and a contact on your networking team (Alice?)
- Week 1: create PrivateLink endpoint in staging + configure NLB in our managed VPC, test connectivity and auth
- Week 2: run 72-hour load run; exercise VPN failover; collect SLO baselines

If you want I can join a 30-minute kickoff Thursday to walk the security checklist.

-Rishi
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
